List the references a database cites

Source: R/get_references.R
get_references.Rd

Lists the references cited by the data in a traits.build database, or in the part of one returned by an extract_*() function, each formatted as a citation. With file, it also writes them to a BibTeX file. Use it to cite the studies behind the data you use.

Usage

get_references(database, file = NULL)

Arguments

database

traits.build database (list object), or the result of an extract_*() function.

file

Path of a BibTeX file to write the references to, or NULL (the default) to write none. An existing file is overwritten. As with RefManageR::WriteBib(), .bib is added to a name that does not end in it.

Value

A tibble with one row per reference, sorted by key in the C locale, and columns:

  • key: the reference's citation key, as in sources.

  • citation: the reference, formatted as in the citation columns of join_sources() and the methods table, or NA when sources has no entry for the key.

  • type: how the data cite it. "dataset": the reference describing a dataset. "source": a study that observations were taken from, in a dataset compiled from several studies. "secondary": a further reference for a dataset, such as a later paper using the same data.

Details

The references are the ones the data cite, read from the traits, excluded data and methods tables: each dataset's own reference, each observation's source_id and each dataset's secondary references. These are also the references extract_data() keeps in sources, so for a database or any extract_*() result the references listed are those in its sources. A key cited in more than one way gets the first type of "dataset", "source" and "secondary".

In databases built with traits.build 2.3 or later, a dataset's own reference is keyed by its dataset_id, and every source_id is a key in sources. In older ones a dataset's own reference is the methods table's source_primary_key, the studies are listed in its source_original_dataset_key, and source_id was free text, so only the values that are keys in sources are read. Each dataset of a database combined with bind_databases() is read by the rules of its own build.

A cited key with no entry in sources is listed with an NA citation and a warning, rather than silently dropped. A database can have such keys when a dataset names a study it took observations from without giving its reference. Only the references in sources are written to file.

A flattened database (one table, see flatten_database()) has no sources, so its references cannot be listed.

See also

join_sources() to add each observation's references to the traits table, traits_build_sources to look up sources by key.

Examples

refs <- austraits_lite %>%
  extract_dataset("Falster_2003") %>%
  get_references()
refs
#> # A tibble: 1 × 3
#>   key          citation                                                    type 
#>   <chr>        <chr>                                                       <chr>
#> 1 Falster_2003 "D. S. Falster and M. Westoby. \"Leaf size and angle vary … data…

# Write the references to a BibTeX file too
bib_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".bib")
refs <- austraits_lite %>%
  extract_taxa(genus = "Eucalyptus") %>%
  get_references(file = bib_file)
head(readLines(bib_file))
#> [1] "@Online{ABRS_2022,"                                                                         
#> [2] "  year = {2022},"                                                                           
#> [3] "  author = {{Australian Biological Resources Study}},"                                      
#> [4] "  title = {{Flora of Australia, Australian Biological Resources Study, Canberra.}},"        
#> [5] "  publisher = {Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water, Canberra.},"
#> [6] "  url = {http://www.ausflora.org.au},"                                                      
unlink(bib_file)
